Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

append

Stack two datasets

Stata 

append using data2

R dplyr 

bind_rows(data1, data2)

Differs from Stata bind_rows() has R type-promotion and attribute rules; .id creates string source identifiers rather than the numeric codes of append, generate().

Stata reference · R reference

1 more examples and alternatives

Stack datasets and record where each row came from

Stata 

append using data2, generate(source)

R dplyr 

dplyr::bind_rows(data1, data2, .id = "source") |> dplyr::mutate(source = as.integer(source) - 1L)

Differs from Stata Uses numeric source IDs: zero for the master and one for the first using dataset, as Stata append, generate() does. bind_rows() has R type-promotion and attribute rules; .id creates string source identifiers rather than the numeric codes of append, generate().

Stata reference · R reference

cross

Every combination of rows from two datasets

Stata 

cross using data2

R dplyr 

cross_join(data1, data2)

Differs from Stata cross_join() suffixes overlapping column names; Stata cross keeps master values for overlapping names. Rename overlaps first to obtain the same columns.

Stata reference · R reference

joinby

All pairs of rows within each id

Stata 

joinby id using data2

R dplyr 

inner_join(data1, data2, by = "id", relationship = "many-to-many")

Differs from Stata dplyr retains overlapping non-key columns with suffixes instead of Stata master values, creates no _merge, and does not enforce a declared 1:1 key constraint.

Stata reference · R reference

merge

Put two datasets side by side by row position

Stata 

merge 1:1 _n using data2

R dplyr 

bind_cols(data1, data2)

Differs from Stata bind_cols() needs matching row counts (or recyclable one-row inputs) and repairs duplicate names; merge 1:1 _n can retain unmatched rows.

Stata reference · R reference

Merge with a match report

Stata 

merge 1:1 id using data2

R tidystata 

stata_merge(data1, data2, "1:1", by = "id")

Like Stata, all rows are kept and a .merge column records the match result. full_join(data1, data2, by = "id") merges without the report.

Stata reference · R reference

One-to-many merge with a match report

Stata 

merge 1:m id using data2

R tidystata 

stata_merge(data1, data2, "1:m", by = "id")

Stata reference · R reference

Many-to-one merge with a match report

Stata 

merge m:1 id using data2

R tidystata 

stata_merge(data1, data2, "m:1", by = "id")

Stata reference · R reference

Keep matched rows only

Stata 

merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(match)

R dplyr 

inner_join(data1, data2, by = "id")

Differs from Stata dplyr retains overlapping non-key columns with suffixes instead of Stata master values, creates no _merge, and does not enforce a declared 1:1 key constraint.

5 more examples and alternatives

Keep all rows of the master data

Stata 

merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(master match)

R dplyr 

left_join(data1, data2, by = "id")

Differs from Stata dplyr retains overlapping non-key columns with suffixes instead of Stata master values, creates no _merge, and does not enforce a declared 1:1 key constraint.

Stata reference · R reference

Keep rows of data1 whose id is not in data2

Stata 

merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(master) keepusing(id) nogenerate

R dplyr 

anti_join(data1, data2, by = "id")

Differs from Stata semi_join()/anti_join() select rows by key membership but do not enforce the unique keys required by Stata merge 1:1; validate uniqueness separately.

Stata reference · R reference

Keep rows of data1 whose id is in data2

Stata 

merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(match) keepusing(id) nogenerate

R dplyr 

semi_join(data1, data2, by = "id")

Differs from Stata semi_join()/anti_join() select rows by key membership but do not enforce the unique keys required by Stata merge 1:1; validate uniqueness separately.

Stata reference · R reference

Keep all rows of the using data

Stata 

merge 1:1 id using data2, keep(using match)

R dplyr 

right_join(data1, data2, by = "id")

Differs from Stata dplyr retains overlapping non-key columns with suffixes instead of Stata master values, creates no _merge, and does not enforce a declared 1:1 key constraint.

Stata reference · R reference

Merge on two keys

Stata 

merge 1:1 id1 id2 using data2, nogenerate

R dplyr 

full_join(data1, data2, by = c("id1", "id2"))

Differs from Stata Variables with the same name in both tables get suffixes; choose them with suffix = c("_data1", "_data2"). dplyr retains overlapping non-key columns with suffixes instead of Stata master values, creates no _merge, and does not enforce a declared 1:1 key constraint.
